items.title: Jillean Williams interviewed by Milt Fillius and Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 20, 1995
items.q: The interviewee discusses the Basie band's spirit, conducting, and alumni events (e.g., 'Mrs. Basie gave them some presentation'), but does not state they were a member of the band or personally worked with Bill Basie.

ctx.x: Do you find that that idea of big bands traveling like they did is kind of a lost thing now? There’s still a few around but, in fact we saw the Basie band about a month ago, but was it a hard life at that point? Because I always wanted to do that. And I always had maybe not a clear picture of what it was really like. © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

I would think it was hard in the sense that, you know, 13 one-nighters in a row in different towns is pretty tough. So from the point of view of sleeping and eating it was hard. But I think that’s what they liked to do because they all loved to play. There was a tremendous spirit of loyalty among the Basie band. And it sort of shows in the way Basie conducts, you know. I mean he only had to point a finger or nod or something and that was his conducting. There was no waving his arms in front of the band. There was…
There’s still that cohesion in the alumni I think.
